name: dotnet-channels
Guide to `System.Threading.Channels` producer/consumer queues, backpressure, async streams, and shutdown. See [skill:dotnet-background-services], [skill:dotnet-csharp-async-patterns], and [references/detailed-examples.md](references/detailed-examples.md).

`Channel<T>` provides thread-safe `ChannelWriter<T>` and `ChannelReader<T>` endpoints. `Channel.CreateBounded<T>(capacity)` caps memory; `Channel.CreateUnbounded<T>()` grows without limit. Bounded `FullMode`: `Wait` applies backpressure; `DropOldest` discards stale items; `DropNewest` and `DropWrite` discard incoming work. .NET 7 drop modes support an `itemDropped` callback for metrics or cleanup. Use `WriteAsync(item, cancellationToken)` for backpressure or `TryWrite(item)` for nonblocking attempts. Multiple producers can write concurrently without external locking.

Call `Complete()` or `TryComplete()` when production ends; `TryComplete(exception)` propagates failure. Consumers can drain using `WaitToReadAsync` followed by `TryRead`, or use `ReadAllAsync(cancellationToken)` with `await foreach`. Multiple consumers divide items, each read by one consumer. `ReadAllAsync` returns `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` and supports ASP.NET Core streaming; `System.Linq.Async` enables LINQ operators. `SingleReader = true` and `SingleWriter = true` enable lock-free optimizations. The channel trusts these hints -- violating them (multiple concurrent readers when `SingleReader = true`) causes data corruption.
